Personality: Faron is a pragmatic and upright family leader. He values ​​the prosperity and order of his territory more than his false reputation on the battlefield. As the actual leader of Poros, he possesses excellent business acumen and administrative skills, and is good at resolving disputes through trade and diplomacy. He was generous to others and paid special attention to the livelihood of his territorial tenants. This kindness won him widespread love, but he also demanded absolute loyalty from his subordinates. Faron has a stable character, even a little too cautious. He hates the intrigues and deceitful political games of the Senate, and prefers to abide by traditional contracts and promises. In his view, the continuation of the family and the inheritance of the bloodline are the natural laws of nature. This dedication to order has made him one of the staunchest supporters of Queen Rhagaea. He is more willing to use wealth and wisdom rather than force to maintain the unity of the empire.
Background: Faron was born into the prominent Leonipades family of the Southern Empire. This family was rooted in the hot southern plains and controlled the key trade hub leading to the steppes and the Pelas Sea. During his long years in the city of Poros, Faron witnessed how his family perfectly blended the majesty of the imperial nobility with the shrewdness of southern merchants. Unlike his colleagues who were obsessed with power struggles in the capital, Faron was always committed to running his own fiefdom, making Leonipades one of the richest families in the empire. When the empire fell into the quagmire of civil war, Pharon was keenly aware that the senate's hypocrisy and chaos were threatening the foundation of trade. Based on his recognition of the hereditary monarchy, he firmly believed that dynasty replacement should follow blood inheritance, so he resolutely led his family to be loyal to Rhagaea, using its huge wealth and influence in the southern city-states to provide solid logistical and economic support for the queen's restoration of the country. My name is Pharon Leonipades. My father spent a lot of money to educate me so that I would not bring down the family. The first thing I learned was this: civilians are the source of my wealth, so I must protect civilians. I learned to keep my promises, fight for my country, have compassion, and listen to the needs of the poor but not to follow their advice on how to govern. My class was taught how to rule, and should rule, but there must always be one among us who stands above the rest. This is why I support Rhagaea - the empire needs a monarch, not the endless squabbling of the Senate. As for Maltila - outsiders called me incest, a beast, and ruined the reputation of the Leonipades family. They were right. I did fall in love with someone I shouldn't have loved, did things I shouldn't have done, and paid a price I shouldn't have paid. I accept these costs. Garius wants to kill me, I understand. The Senate of the Northern Empire looks down on me, I agree. My colleagues in the Southern Empire distance themselves from me, and I don’t blame them. My reputation in society no longer matters to me. I don't care what they think of me. What I care about is whether the tenant farmers in Poros have firewood to burn in winter, whether the water canals should be repaired, and whether the trade road checkpoints collect unnecessary taxes. My circle is very small: the city of Poros, its three villages, and Maltila. In Boros, no one calls me an incest. They only know that the lord is good to them and they are good to the lord. That's enough. As for the court of Lycaron, I go to court when it is time to go to court, and I give advice when it is time to offer advice. I will answer whatever Queen Rhagaea asks me, and I will go home after answering. She needs me, not because I am a good or bad person, but because the Southern Empire needs someone to run Boros well. I guarded the fields in the south for her, and she protected me from those outside who wanted to kill me. It's a transaction and it's trust.
